projects.name: Policy and regulatory frameworks and institutional capacity strengthened to address informality
projects.description:
1. An integrated strategy for formalisation is drafted by the ILO, based on the analysis on informality and other knowledge generated by this RBSA-funded initiative, evidence shared by other UN agencies (e.g., situation analyses by IOM and WFP) and social dialogue through the taskforce meetings. Policies and measures are designed to improve working conditions of women in the informal economy and promote their formalisation. Capacity of enterprises and local government is built to boost productivity and create more formal jobs and facilitate transition to the formality and a greener economy. This initiative strengthens the capacity of USS to facilitate transition from informal to formal employment and help job place displaced workers. This will help prevent informalisation of the labour market as it increases the resilience of the labour market to withstand the downward pressure due to an influx of displaced population into Armenia. Responding to a request of the ministry of labour and social affairs, the RBSA-funded initiative will revise the staff qualification framework of USS and revamp induction and up-skilling training packages. It also trains USS staff members so they can plan, implement, and monitor public works schemes that also benefit women jobseekers.
A tripartite and inter-ministerial taskforce is established as a platform of social dialogue while assuring gender-balance of the taskforce members. The taskforce is expected to draw up a national strategy to address informality in a coordinated manner as described in the next point. This initiative conducts a gap analysis and provide technical assistance in view of ratification of the C102 as extension of social security coverage helps formalisation of informal employment.
2. The capacity of social partners will be strengthened to support refugees’ access to formal employment and reach out informal economic units and informal workers, especially women-headed enterprises and women informal workers.

projects.name: The Ministry of Environment has a strengthened capacity to fulfill commitment under the Vienna Convention on the Protection of the Ozone Layer and the Montreal Protocol on Substances that Deplete the Ozone Layer
projects.description:
Institutional strengthening projects have been funded by the Executive Committee since its seventh meeting to provide financial support to Article 5 countries to enhance national capacities for the timely and effective implementation of ozone-depleting substances (ODS) phase-out activities. These projects support coordination between the concerned country, the Executive Committee, the Multilateral Fund Secretariat and the implementing agencies, and have been instrumental in ensuring broad compliance with the Montreal Protocol.

In Armenia, the institutional strengthening project pursues several interrelated objectives. These include the adoption and implementation of legislation and regulations to control and monitor the import and use of Montreal Protocol controlled substances and related equipment; the accurate and timely collection and reporting of data on the consumption of all Montreal Protocol controlled substances; and the strengthening of coordination among national agencies and stakeholders in support of the objectives of the Montreal Protocol. The project also supports oversight of the timely implementation of hydrochlorofluorocarbon (HCFC) phase-out and hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) phase-down activities and the associated reductions in the consumption of controlled substances. In addition, it promotes awareness-raising and information exchange on Montreal Protocol-related issues and supports regional cooperation and participation in Montreal Protocol processes.

projects.name: The Kigali HFC implementation plan is developed
projects.description:
The Kigali hydrofluorocarbon (HFC) implementation plan, stage I, provides a strategic framework to support Armenia in reducing its consumption of hydrofluorocarbons, which are potent greenhouse gases widely used in refrigeration and air-conditioning. Through implementation of the plan, Armenia aims to achieve a 10% reduction from its HFC baseline consumption by 1 January 2029, in line with the obligations of the Kigali Amendment and its global objective to reduce HFC use by 80% by 2045.

The plan comprises a comprehensive set of measures, including regulatory updates, improvements in industry practices and the promotion of environmentally friendly alternative technologies. Through these coordinated actions, Armenia will strengthen its compliance with international commitments under the Kigali Amendment while contributing to global climate change mitigation efforts.
